evidence.label: mcp-go-shell-exec-interpreter (critical/medium)
evidence.detail: A shell interpreter is invoked with a constructed command string. Go's exec.Command is safe by default precisely because it takes an argument vector; routing through `sh -c` gives that safety away.

evidence.label: mcp-js-prototype-pollution-merge-loop (medium/medium)
evidence.detail: Keys from a caller-supplied object are copied onto a target without excluding __proto__ / constructor / prototype. A tool argument carrying __proto__ then mutates Object.prototype for the whole process, which can turn an unrelated later property read into attacker-controlled data.

evidence.label: mcp-go-sql-string-built (medium/low)
evidence.detail: Listed, not deducted: this check is new and its precision has not been measured, so it is shown for review and scores nothing. A SQL statement is assembled by string building — fmt.Sprintf, or concatenation with something that is not a constant — and passed straight to a query method. A value built in can always be sent as an argument after the statement instead (database/sql, pgx and sqlx all take them), and a caller-supplied one is SQL injection; an identifier (a table or column name) cannot be an argument and must be validated or quoted. This check cannot tell which the built part is, so it is listed for review, not deducted.
evidence.excerpt:
func (d *DB) NextSequence(table, prefix string) (int, error) {
	var maxNum int
	err := d.db.QueryRow(fmt.Sprintf(
		"SELECT COALESCE(MAX(CAST(SUBSTR(id, ?) AS INTEGER)), 0) FROM %s WHERE id LIKE ?",
		table), len(prefix)+2, prefix+"-%").Scan(&maxNum)
